title: ROUND vs MROUND: to decimals or to a multiple
meta_desc: ROUND vs MROUND: rounding to decimal places versus rounding to the nearest multiple (0.25, 5, 15 minutes). When each fits, plus negative-number notes.
intro: ROUND snaps to a number of decimal PLACES; MROUND snaps to the nearest MULTIPLE of whatever you give it. "Round to 2 decimals" is ROUND; "round to the nearest quarter / nickel / 15 minutes" is MROUND. Choosing by the unit you're thinking in makes the formula read itself.

cols: The nearest multiple of a value
MROUND(x,5) for nearest 5, MROUND(x,1) = nearest integer
Number and multiple must share a sign, or MROUND errors (#NUM!)
Universal (both verified in every version we test)

when.use_when: Decimal precision: currency to cents (2 places), trimming display noise, ROUND(x,-2) for the nearest hundred. It's the everyday rounder.
Real-world increments: prices to the nearest 0.05 or 0.25, quantities to case sizes, and time to 15-minute blocks with MROUND(t,TIME(0,15,0)). Anything sold or billed in fixed steps.

compat_note: Both execute identically in every LibreOffice build and in the Google Sheets run we execute (desktop Excel per Microsoft's docs — we do not run desktop Excel). One MROUND gotcha that's the same everywhere: the value and the multiple must have the same sign — MROUND(-7,5) errors, MROUND(-7,-5) is fine. For forced-direction multiple rounding, CEILING and FLOOR are the cousins (see ROUNDUP vs CEILING). Excel for the web is a separate application with its own calculation engine, and that one we do execute: all 9 corpus cases for these functions matched the documented values there (recalculated on OneDrive, 2026-09-01); the per-case values are on the individual function pages.
